d.title: Same operation, opposite effect
d.caption: For a linear model, binning turns one coefficient into one per bin — a step function that can follow any shape. For a tree, binning removes the ability to split anywhere inside an interval: it can now only cut at your edges. Which model is downstream decides whether this is a feature or a handicap.

d.title: Free text with structure inside
d.caption: A free-text field that people fill in by hand is rarely free of structure — it holds a measurement, a code, a unit or a date in whatever format the writer chose. Extracting the structure is worth more than vectorising the text, and the pattern that matched is itself a feature.
cells: blank is not the same as "n/a"

d.title: Three things a pipeline cannot do
d.caption: A pipeline is a chain of **row-preserving** transforms followed by a model: `transform` must return as many rows as it received. Everything that changes the row count, or that needs other rows, lives outside it — and knowing where that work goes is what keeps it from drifting between training and serving.

d.title: The threshold is a business decision, not a model output
d.caption: The probabilities already contain the ranking; what the default 0.5 gets wrong is where to cut it. On a 1% positive rate almost nothing clears 0.5, so the model predicts the majority class everywhere and reports 99% accuracy — having learned nothing.
